cohort: The study participants were full-term infants in the United States from 2010 to 2018, with a focus on those diagnosed with Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) and their racial backgrounds.
finding: African American neonates had a significantly higher likelihood of developing and experiencing severe HIE, as well as higher overall mortality, while Native American infants were less likely to receive hypothermia therapy compared to Caucasian infants.
